subject: Storage rules: what we persist vs ephemeral for requests & outputs
messages:
From: Elaine Gupta <elaine.gupta@brightbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on what Redwood persists by default

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightBank is evaluating Redwood for powering several internal agents. Two quick, slightly technical questions that our InfoSec team asked me to confirm:

1) By default, what categories of items do you persist from an API request? In particular: original customer request (prompt), model-generated outputs, and any intermediate derivatives (token-level logs, embeddings, KV cache snapshots).

2) If data is retained, where is it stored by default (region/residency)? Can we ensure EU-only residency for EU-labeled requests?

We can sign an NDA but wanted to get the default behavior in writing before escalating to procurement. I've attached our SOC checklist to show the fields they care about.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with the InfoSec owner.

Best,
Elaine
Senior Product Security Manager
BrightBank

Attachments: SOC2-Snapshot-2025.pdf (pdf), brightbank-checklist.xlsx (referenced)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Gupta <elaine.gupta@brightbank.com>
Cc: k arthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood persists by default

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear questions and the checklist. Summary up front: by default Redwood stores the full request and the generated response for hosted API usage for up to 45 days (used for telemetry, quality monitoring, and abuse detection). Ephemeral intermediate artifacts such as KV cache are not persisted beyond the request lifecycle in hosted mode. EU-only residency can be enforced per-customer (we can pin their data region).

Detailed bullets below so you can paste into your InfoSec note:
- Default capture: request payload (prompt + metadata) and model output(s). These are captured for 45 days by default for hosted customers.
- Derivatives: embeddings or token-level debug artifacts are not stored by default unless a customer explicitly enables features that generate them (e.g., "store-embeddings" flag or debug logging).
- KV cache / runtime caches: not persisted to durable storage in hosted mode; they live in-memory and are dropped after the request completes.
- Residency: hosted API defaults to region of the nearest Redwood cluster; we offer customer configuration to pin all storage to EU-only or US-only regions for enterprise customers.
- Opt-out: customers can enable a "no-persist" mode at the API key level which disables capture of prompts/outputs for their traffic; note this disables some observability features and prevents retrospective evals.

I'm looping in Karthik to confirm the precise retention window language for enterprise contracts and Marissa for the audit evidence we can share.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Elaine Gupta <elaine.gupta@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood persists by default

Elaine — adding contractual / SLA nuance: for self-serve hosted customers we document a 45-day default retention for requests+responses. For Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, retention is controlled by the customer's environment and can be configured to shorter windows or immediate purge; we can add an explicit term in the MSA to enforce EU-only storage and retention windows.

One caveat: if a customer asks us to enable advanced features (long-term vector stores, persistent conversation history, or manual evaluation pipelines), those features will store artifacts beyond the default window — we surface this in the feature enablement flow and in the contract.

If BrightBank needs EU-only retention plus automated purges after X days, we can add that as a contractual requirement and provide the relevant Runbook for deletion + audit logs.

-Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions

(Internal note: Marissa, can you prepare the deletion runbook and last-12-months audit snapshot we can safely share?)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Elaine Gupta <elaine.gupta@brightbank.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T13:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood persists by default

Elaine — attached is a concise runbook we typically share with prospects; highlights in plain language for your InfoSec team:
- Default retention: 45 days for request+response for hosted customers; system is TTL-driven and purges automatically.
- Prompts vs outputs: both are treated as "request artifacts" and purged on the same schedule unless customer-specified features override that.
- Opt-out: API key-level "no_persist" disables capture; for production traffic we recommend a scoped approach (exclude sensitive flows) rather than full disable.
- Audit trail: when we run a purge we emit audit events and a purge report; for enterprise customers we can deliver a signed purge affidavit upon request.

I'll also include a sanitized sample of the purge log and the SOC2 evidence pack via secure link.

-M

From: Elaine Gupta <elaine.gupta@brightbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood persists by default

Thanks team — this is exactly what we needed. A couple very small follow-ups from InfoSec after reviewing your notes:

1) Can you confirm whether debug-level token logs are ever written to durable storage during incident investigations? If yes, what controls (access logs, retention) apply?
2) For the API key-level no_persist option: will usage metrics (counts, latency histograms) still be captured in aggregate (not payload-level)? We need telemetry for SLOs but cannot accept payload retention.

If you can send two short bullet answers we can close the SOC intake and move to the procurement data sheet stage.

Best,
Elaine
